news.headline: RBI MPC Decision at 10 AM IST — 25bps Rate Hike to 5.50% Expected
news.what_happened: The RBI Monetary Policy Committee concludes its Oct 5-7 meeting today with the decision due at 10:00 AM IST. In a Reuters poll of 61 economists, 35 expect a 25bps hike from 5.25% to 5.50% — the first rate hike after 125bps of cuts in 2025. Retail inflation at 4.82%, Brent crude above $100/bbl, and rupee weakening beyond 96 are cited drivers.
news.why_it_matters: A rate hike would end the accommodative cycle and directly pressure rate-sensitive sectors: private and PSU banks, NBFCs, housing finance, real estate, and auto loans. The entire market is in wait-and-watch mode until 10 AM. A surprise hold would trigger a sharp relief rally in banking and NBFC stocks.

news.headline: Brent Crude Breaks Above $100/bbl — WTI at $90.24 (+0.89%)
news.what_happened: Brent crude rose to $101.40/bbl (+0.82%) and WTI climbed to $90.24/bbl (+0.89%). OPEC+ members reaffirmed output discipline with Iraq pledging deeper cuts to compensate for earlier overproduction. Geopolitical premium sustained.
news.why_it_matters: Brent above $100 widens India's current account deficit and reinforces the inflationary case for RBI's rate hike. Upstream oil companies (ONGC, OIL) earn higher per-barrel realization. OMCs (BPCL, HPCL, IOC) gain from inventory re-valuation. Airlines, paints, tyres, and chemicals face direct input cost pressure.

news.headline: India-US Trade Deal: Generic Pharma Explicitly Exempt from 100% Tariff
news.what_happened: Under Trump's executive order (April 2026), a 100% tariff applies to branded/patented pharmaceuticals but generic medicines, biosimilars, and their inputs are explicitly exempted. The India-US bilateral deal (Feb 2026) set the effective overall tariff on Indian goods to 18%, down from 25%.
news.why_it_matters: India exports approximately $8 billion in generic drugs to the US annually — one-third of total pharma exports. The generic exemption removes the biggest regulatory overhang for Indian pharma in 2026. SUNPHARMA, DRREDDY, CIPLA, LUPIN, and DIVISLAB retain full US market access and competitive advantage.

news.headline: Asian Markets Weak — Nikkei -0.93%, Hang Seng -0.78%
news.what_happened: Japanese and Hong Kong markets fell sharply as rising crude prices and tighter global monetary conditions raised growth concerns. Nikkei fell to 70,024 (-0.93%), Hang Seng fell to 24,090 (-0.78%). Cumulative GIFT Nifty decline of ~93 points signals gap-down opening.
news.why_it_matters: Negative Asian cues compound India's domestic rate hike anxiety. Metals sector is particularly vulnerable on weak China/Asia demand signals. GIFT Nifty at 22,683 (-0.41%) suggests Nifty 50 opens ~93 points lower from yesterday's close of 22,776.

picks.catalyst: Brent crude breaks above $100/bbl (+0.82%), Natural Gas +0.77%
picks.logic: ONGC's upstream realization tracks international crude benchmarks directly. With Brent at $101.40, every $1 rise adds approximately Rs 800-1000 Cr to annual earnings. Rising natural gas prices add a second tailwind. This is the cleanest crude play with no regulatory cap on realization — Q2FY27 results (upcoming) will benefit significantly from today's commodity levels.

picks.catalyst: Brent crude above $100/bbl — OMC inventory re-valuation gains
picks.logic: BPCL holds large crude oil and petroleum product inventories. When crude prices rise, the inventory already purchased at lower prices gains in value — these inventory gains flow directly to quarterly profits. Brent rising above the key $100 threshold is a clear P&L catalyst. Prev close Rs 296.95; gap-down open may offer entry near watch zone.

picks.catalyst: India-US trade deal: generic pharma exempt from 100% US tariff; defensive sector in rate-hike environment
picks.logic: Sun Pharma earns approximately 30% of its revenue from US generics — India's core pharma export. Trump's 100% tariff on patented drugs explicitly excludes generics, removing the biggest regulatory overhang for Indian pharma in 2026. Additionally, pharma is a defensive sector: as banking, real estate, and auto rotate lower on RBI rate hike, fund flows shift to defensives like pharma and FMCG.
